title: Catalogue of transparent injected preparations — sold by Smith and Beck, London
citation: [Unsigned editorial note], “Catalogue of transparent injected preparations — sold by Smith and Beck, London,” Quarterly Journal of Microscopical Science, new series 1 (1861): 129–131.
tags: Smith & Beck; Karl Thiersch; transparent injections; histology slides; trade; catalogue
note: A period source devoted to a commercial series of mounted transparent-injection slides offered by Smith & Beck. The note reports on preparations supplied for sale and is directly tied to the surviving German injection mounts later attributed to Karl Thiersch. It is admitted as an object-and-trade source, not as general periodical microscopy.
links: Howard Lynk reconstruction and bibliography: https://microscopist.net/Thiersch.html; Brian Bracegirdle source survey / DOI: https://doi.org/10.1177/007327537701500201

authors: Brian Stevenson, Brian Davidson, Peter Paisley, and Howard Lynk
title: Nineteenth-century microscope slide mounters JWB and JB: their work and their identities
citation: Brian Stevenson, Brian Davidson, Peter Paisley, and Howard Lynk, “Nineteenth-century microscope slide mounters JWB and JB: their work and their identities,” Quekett Journal of Microscopy 41 (2010): 203–217.
tags: James William Bond; John Barnett; JWB; JB; slide makers; handwriting; labels; retail; attribution
note: A maker-attribution study built from surviving slides. Monograms, handwriting, paper patterns and retailers’ secondary labels are used to identify JWB as James William Bond and JB as John Barnett and to reconstruct their commercial production.
links: Quekett Microscopical Club contents: https://www.quekett.org/about/journal/contents/journal-41; James William Bond research page: https://microscopist.net/BondJW.html; John Barnett research page: https://microscopist.net/BarnettJ.html

authors: Rudolf Staroscik and Brian M. Davidson
title: Parry’s soundings
citation: Rudolf Staroscik and Brian M. Davidson, “Parry’s soundings,” Quekett Journal of Microscopy 41 (2011): 531–542.
tags: deep-sea slides; soundings; labels; provenance; John Ross; William Parry; surviving slides
note: A slide-provenance investigation centred on surviving preparations labelled as Parry soundings. The authors test the labels against expedition records and reconstruct the collection history of early deep-sea sounding material, making the physical slides the evidentiary problem rather than an illustration of expedition history.
links: Quekett Microscopical Club contents: https://www.quekett.org/about/journal/contents/journal-41; Bonhams catalogue summary of the published reconstruction: https://www.the-saleroom.com/en-gb/price-guide/the-who?page=1814

title: The 1860s Smith, Beck & Beck transparent injections
citation: Howard Lynk, “The 1860s Smith, Beck & Beck transparent injections,” Quekett Journal of Microscopy 41 (2012): 701–712.
tags: Smith Beck & Beck; Karl Thiersch; transparent injections; imported slides; labels; trade; attribution
note: Object-led reconstruction of the distinctive transparent-injection slides sold by Smith, Beck & Beck in the early 1860s. Surviving mounts, label forms, preparation techniques, advertisements and delivery records are combined to identify Karl Thiersch as the maker and to trace the slides as German imports retailed in Britain.
links: Quekett Microscopical Club contents: https://www.quekett.org/about/journal/contents/journal-41; author’s expanded reconstruction: https://microscopist.net/Thiersch.html

title: Humanembryologische Schnittseriensammlungen um 1900 am Beispiel der Marburger Gasser-Strahl’schen Sammlung
citation: Caroline Maria Stiel, Humanembryologische Schnittseriensammlungen um 1900 am Beispiel der Marburger Gasser-Strahl’schen Sammlung, Beiträge zur Wissenschafts- und Medizingeschichte 11 (Berlin: Peter Lang, 2023). https://doi.org/10.3726/b20501.
tags: Gasser-Strahl; serial sections; histological slides; Marburg; embryology; provenance; circulation; loans
note: A physical-collection history of a human-embryological serial-section collection made at Marburg from 1887 to 1923. The study starts from a collection originally exceeding 10,000 glass slides with sections from 147 embryos and fetuses and reconstructs acquisition, processing, naming, research use, loans and present condition.
